chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Writing "Lover Man" and "Mad About You" for Barnet
summary: The songs, with lyrics by Jimmy Davis and Walter Bishop Sr., were recorded in Kirby's Larry Adler album; Willie Dukes imitated Billie Holiday.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: By this time the record was breaking. Kirby and I, we did Larry Adler's album, and for doing Larry Adler's album they took two numbers, "Mad About You" and "Lover Man." This is while I was in Kirby's...
Were these the first sort of numbers you made the name with?
Well, when did you write them?

I wrote those songs for Charlie Barnet. "Mad About You" Walter Bishop Senior did the lyrics for. I wrote "Lover Man" and Jimmy Davis did the lyrics for that. Apparently, in those days, the only... There was a singer by the name of Willie Dukes. We always called him Day-to-Day, you know. But he was the only one that really made it on 52nd Street and sang with various groups. And he sang like Billie Holiday. Well, he started at Monroe's Uptown House, which I played now and then also; that's where Charlie Parker started. I was at the Uptown House before Charlie came to New York. Because I'm a New Yorker; I'm here... So what am I getting to?
